d: Role Description The Director will provide strategic and academic leadership for ICAMMDA, overseeing research programs, training activities, and partnerships focused on applied mathematical modelling and data analytics for malaria and NTDs. This full-time remote role involves setting research priorities, supervising multidisciplinary teams, mentoring early-career researchers, and ensuring high-quality outputs that inform policy and practice. The Director will coordinate collaboration with international and local partners, manage grants and funding streams, and represent the Centre in regional and global forums. Daily responsibilities include reviewing project progress, guiding model development and data analysis, supporting curriculum and workshop design, and fostering a culture of ethical, rigorous, and inclusive research. The Director will also contribute to publications, proposal writing, stakeholder engagement with NMCPs and NGOs, and long-term capacity development across the WAMCAD network.
q: Advanced expertise in applied mathematics, statistics, or epidemiology, with demonstrated experience in infectious disease modelling (malaria and/or NTDs preferred).
Strong skills in data analytics and quantitative methods, including handling large datasets, model calibration, and interpretation of results for decision-making.
Experience in academic or research leadership, including supervising teams, mentoring researchers, and managing multi-institutional projects.
Proven ability to secure and manage research funding, with familiarity in grant writing, budgeting, and reporting to international donors.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to present complex technical concepts to technical and non-technical audiences.
Demonstrated experience working with or alongside public health agencies, NGOs, or National Malaria Control Programmes, and an interest in global health policy.
Strong collaboration and partnership-building skills, with the ability to work effectively across cultures and disciplines in remote, distributed teams.

d: Located in Doha, Qatar, GEMS American Academy Qatar (GAAQ) delivers a high-quality education through the American Common Core curriculum, preparing students to thrive academically and become successful global citizens.

At GAAQ, we believe the very best schools develop learners who are purposeful, tenacious, innovative, and respectful leaders. These values underpin everything we do, creating an inclusive learning environment where students are challenged to achieve excellence while developing the skills and character needed for success beyond the classroom.

As part of the global GEMS Education network, GAAQ offers educators the opportunity to work within one of the world's leading private education providers, with access to outstanding professional development and career advancement opportunities.
We are seeking an outstanding and passionate Female Early Years Physical Education Teacher to join our team from November 2026.

The successful candidate will inspire a love of Kindergarten/Early Years PE, deliver engaging lessons that challenge and support every learner, and contribute positively to the wider life of our vibrant school community.
We are particularly interested in educators with experience teaching within the American curriculum, who understand its distinct approach to teaching, learning, and assessment.
q: A Bachelor of Education or a Bachelor's degree in Early Years or Elementary education (or Physical Education), together with a state teaching license, PGCE, or equivalent recognized teaching qualification.
A minimum of two years' experience teaching Elementary PE at the Elementary/Lower School level.
Experience teaching within the American curriculum, with a strong understanding of American educational standards, teaching methodologies, and assessment practices.
Native or near-native proficiency in English, with excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong subject knowledge and a passion for delivering outstanding teaching and learning.
Confidence in using technology to enhance student engagement and learning outcomes.
A commitment to continuous professional development and contributing to the wider school community.
A genuine alignment with the GEMS Core Values of Respect, Innovation, Leadership, Purpose, and Tenacity.

If you are passionate about education and ready to take the next step in your international teaching career, we would love to hear from you.
To apply, please submit your updated CV through the GEMS Education Careers website.
Please note that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted regarding the next steps in the recruitment process.

GEMS Education is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. We are dedicated to creating safe, supportive, and inclusive learning environments where students can thrive, and we expect all employees, volunteers, and partners to share this commitment.

As part of our safer recruitment practices, all successful applicants will be subject to comprehensive pre-employment checks, including verification of identity, qualifications, employment history, professional references, and criminal record checks from all countries of residence and employment, in line with local and international safeguarding requirements. These checks may include enhanced disclosure, prohibition, barring, and overseas police clearance checks where applicable. We are committed to recruiting individuals who uphold the highest standards of professional conduct and child protection.
